question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Hektic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hektic" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "hectic", meaning full of frantic activity; very busy and fast-paced. (अत्यधिक व्यस्त)

◦ Example: She had a hectic week at the office.

• Spelling key: HEC + TIC (with a "c", not a "k").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are correctly spelt: "Gentle" (mild/soft), "Brilliant" (very bright/clever) and "Kinetic" (relating to motion).

NOTE

• Words ending in the /k/ sound are often spelt "-ic" in English: hectic, kinetic, frantic, drastic, elastic. The spelling "-ktic" is not used.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who is mentally ill
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Lunatic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "lunatic" is a person who is mentally ill (insane). (पागल / विक्षिप्त व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: In earlier times, asylums were built to house lunatics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mercenary" — a soldier who fights for money for a foreign army.

• Option 2 "Psychiatrist" — a doctor who treats mental illness (not one who is ill).

• Option 4 "Psychologist" — a person who studies the mind and human behaviour.

NOTE

• Do not confuse: a psychiatrist is a medical doctor (MBBS) who can prescribe medicines, while a psychologist studies behaviour and provides counselling/therapy.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The company's new product received affirmative feedback from customers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. positive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Affirmative" means agreeing, approving or saying 'yes'; positive. So "affirmative feedback" is favourable, encouraging feedback. Its closest synonym here is "positive". (सकारात्मक / स्वीकारात्मक)

◦ Example: The audience gave an affirmative/positive response to the proposal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "critical" (finding fault) is nearly the opposite in this context.

• Option 3 "detailed" (thorough) and Option 4 "reflective" (thoughtful) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of affirmative: positive, favourable, approving, assenting. Antonyms: negative, dissenting. In grammar, an "affirmative sentence" is a positive (non-negative) statement.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She told me / her name but / I'm not remembering / it now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. I'm not remembering.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Remember" is a stative (non-continuous) verb — verbs of mental state are not normally used in the continuous (-ing) form. So "I'm not remembering" is wrong; it should be "I don't remember".

◦ Correct: She told me her name but I don't remember it now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "She told me", "her name but" and "it now" are all grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Common stative verbs not used in the continuous form: know, remember, understand, believe, like, love, hate, want, need, prefer, belong, own, seem. We say "I know", not "I am knowing".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

He bought strange vintage car on auction from the customs department.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. strange vintage car.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Car" is a singular countable noun and needs an article. The segment should be "a strange vintage car" (using the indefinite article "a").

◦ Correct: He bought a strange vintage car at auction from the customs department.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• A singular countable noun cannot stand alone without a determiner (a/an/the/this/my, etc.).

• (Note also that idiomatically we say "at auction", but the marked error segment is the missing article.)

NOTE

• Use "a" before a consonant sound (a car, a strange car) and "an" before a vowel sound (an auction, an hour). Singular countable nouns almost always need an article or other determiner.

question:
Select the most appropriate phrase to replace the underlined word.

She is feeling unwell today, so she will not be going to work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. under the weather.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "under the weather" means feeling unwell / slightly ill. It correctly replaces "unwell". (अस्वस्थ / तबीयत ठीक न होना)

◦ Correct: She is feeling under the weather today, so she will not be going to work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "head in the clouds" (day-dreaming, out of touch with reality).

• Option 2 "face like thunder" (looking very angry).

• Option 3 "chase rainbows" (pursue unrealistic goals). None mean "unwell".

NOTE

• Other idioms for being ill: "off colour", "out of sorts", "at death's door" (very seriously ill), "feeling green".

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

Just when they reach the airport, the flight had departed from the runway.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Just before they reached.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause uses the past perfect ("had departed"), so the other action must be in the simple past and must logically come after the departure. "Just before they reached" the airport, the flight had (already) departed — the sequence and tenses now agree.

◦ Correct: Just before they reached the airport, the flight had departed from the runway.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "have reached" (present perfect) clashes with the past "had departed".

• Options 2 and 3 use the present tense "reach", which does not match the past narrative.

NOTE

• Past perfect (had + V3) shows the earlier of two past actions; the later action takes the simple past. Here the departure (had departed) happened before they reached (simple past).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Sathish remained unwavering in the face of the assaulting gang, standing as resolute as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. steel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The simile "as resolute as steel" (firm and unshakeable like steel) fits the sense of remaining "unwavering". "Steel" is a strong, hard metal used to suggest firmness and determination. (फ़ौलाद की तरह दृढ़)

◦ Correct: ... standing as resolute as steel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "still" (motionless/quiet), Option 3 "stall" (a booth / to delay) and Option 4 "steal" (to take without permission) are homophones/near-homophones that do not fit.

NOTE

• "Steel" is also used as a verb: "to steel oneself" means to prepare mentally for something difficult. Note the homophone "steal" (to rob).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She confided in me on her anxious, whispering her secrets between sips of coffee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. about her anxiety.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "confided in me" we need the preposition "about" followed by a noun. "Anxious" is an adjective; the correct noun form is "anxiety". So the segment becomes "about her anxiety". (अपनी चिंता के बारे में)

◦ Correct: She confided in me about her anxiety, whispering her secrets between sips of coffee.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 keeps the wrong preposition "on".

• Option 2 uses the adjective "anxious" where a noun is needed.

• Option 4 "regarding herself's anxiousness" is grammatically incorrect ("herself's" is not a valid possessive).

NOTE

• Word forms: adjective anxious → noun anxiety / anxiousness → adverb anxiously. "Confide in (a person) about (something)".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word.

As long as I live, I shall be obliged to my Uncle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. thankless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Obliged" (here) means grateful/thankful/indebted to someone for their help. Its antonym is "thankless" — showing no gratitude / ungrateful. (कृतघ्न — आभारी का विलोम)

◦ Example: I am much obliged (grateful) to you for your help.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "grateful", 2 "pleased" and 4 "indebted" are synonyms of obliged, not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of obliged: grateful, indebted, beholden, thankful. Antonyms: thankless, ungrateful, unappreciative. "Thankless" can also mean a task that earns no thanks (a thankless job).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

I had never saw/ such a sight/ before I visited Switzerland.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I had never saw.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the auxiliary "had", the past participle (V3) is required. The past participle of "see" is "seen" (see – saw – seen), not "saw" (which is the simple past). So it should be "I had never seen".

◦ Correct: I had never seen such a sight before I visited Switzerland.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "such a sight" and "before I visited Switzerland" are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Past perfect = had + past participle (V3): had seen, had gone, had done. Never use the simple past (saw, went, did) after "had".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Please bring some milk from ______ refrigerator in the kitchen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• We use the definite article "the" for a specific, identified thing — here, one particular refrigerator ("in the kitchen"). Both speaker and listener know which one is meant. (निश्चित वस्तु के लिए "the")

◦ Correct: Please bring some milk from the refrigerator in the kitchen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "a/an" are indefinite articles used for a non-specific single thing; they do not fit a particular, known refrigerator.

• Omitting the article ("No article required") is wrong because a singular countable noun needs a determiner.

NOTE

• Use "the" when the noun is unique, already mentioned, or made specific by a phrase like "in the kitchen"; use "a/an" when mentioning a singular countable noun for the first time or in a general sense.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Though Amal took continuous medication, he was not able to __________________ his injury.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. heal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Heal" means to make (a wound/injury) healthy again; to cure. It correctly fits "his injury". (घाव भरना / स्वस्थ करना)

◦ Correct: Though Amal took continuous medication, he was not able to heal his injury.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "heel" (the back part of the foot), Option 3 "hail" (frozen rain / to greet) and Option 4 "hill" (a small mountain) are homophones/near-homophones that do not fit.

NOTE

• Homophones: heal (to cure) vs heel (part of foot); hail (ice pellets / to greet) vs hale (healthy, as in "hale and hearty").

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Wine glass is very fragile; you must handle it with care.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Delicate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fragile" means easily broken or damaged; delicate. Its closest synonym is "delicate". (नाज़ुक / आसानी से टूटने वाला)

◦ Example: The fragile/delicate vase shattered when it fell.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Resilient" (able to recover quickly / spring back) and Option 2 "Sturdy" (strong, tough) are antonyms.

• Option 4 "Rough" (not smooth) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fragile: delicate, brittle, frail, flimsy. Antonyms: sturdy, robust, tough, durable, resilient.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined idiom/phrase in the given sentence.

The salesman informed the customers that if they had any questions, they could drop a line.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. send a brief letter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "drop a line" means to send a short letter, note or message to someone. So it can be substituted by "send a brief letter". (संक्षिप्त पत्र/संदेश भेजना)

◦ Example: Drop me a line when you reach home safely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "complain against him", 3 "call his secretary" and 4 "come back with the items" do not carry the meaning of the idiom.

NOTE

• Related communication idioms: "drop a line" (send a short message), "give someone a ring/buzz" (phone someone), "touch base" (make contact briefly).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Tara has been playing / cricket with her friends / since noon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is grammatically correct. It uses the present perfect continuous ("has been playing") for an action that started in the past and is still continuing, with "since" correctly marking a point of time ("since noon").

◦ Correct: Tara has been playing cricket with her friends since noon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "has been playing" (present perfect continuous) is correct for a singular subject "Tara".

• "since noon" correctly uses "since" with a point of time.

NOTE

• Present perfect continuous = has/have been + verb-ing. Use "since" with a point of time (since noon, since Monday) and "for" with a length of time (for two hours).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error.

Surprisingly!/ dark chocolates/ are most bitterer/ in taste.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. are most bitterer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Most bitterer" is a double error: it wrongly combines the superlative marker "most" with the comparative "bitterer". The comparative degree of "bitter" is "bitterer" (or "more bitter") and the superlative is "bitterest" (or "most bitter"). Here the correct form should simply be "bitterer" (comparative) or "more bitter".

◦ Correct: Surprisingly, dark chocolates are bitterer (more bitter) in taste.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Never mix "more/most" with the "-er/-est" ending (no "most bitterer", "more better").

NOTE

• Degrees of "bitter": bitter – bitterer / more bitter – bitterest / most bitter. Use the comparative with "than" and the superlative with "the".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

His business was so successful that Mark was able to _________ at the age of 50.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. retire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Retire" means to stop working (usually because of age) after a long career. As the business was very successful, Mark could afford to retire at 50. (सेवानिवृत्त होना)

◦ Correct: His business was so successful that Mark was able to retire at the age of 50.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "admit" (to confess/allow entry), Option 2 "give up" (to quit/surrender) and Option 3 "succeed" (to achieve success) do not fit the idea of stopping work after success.

NOTE

• "Retire" (stop working) vs "retreat" (withdraw). Related nouns: retirement, retiree. "Give up" implies quitting due to failure, which contradicts "so successful".

question:
Select the option that rectifies the underlined spelling error.

The permisible limit of vehicle speed has been increased in India by the Road Transport Corporation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. permissible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "permissible", meaning allowed / permitted. The word in the sentence ("permisible") is misspelt. (अनुमेय / स्वीकार्य)

◦ Correct: The permissible limit of vehicle speed has been increased in India ...

• Spelling key: PER + MISS + IBLE (double "s", ends in "-ible").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2's "parmissible", Option 3's "parmitted" and Option 4's "permisibble" are all misspelt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Permissible" comes from "permit"; note the double "s" and the "-ible" ending (not "-able").

NOTE

• Related words: permit (verb/noun), permission (noun), permissible (adjective). Common "-ible" words: possible, visible, permissible, sensible, edible.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence.

As the roller coaster reached its highest point, a surge of addrenalline coursed through her veins, making her heart race with excitement.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. adrenaline.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "adrenaline" — a hormone (also called epinephrine) released by the adrenal glands that increases heart rate and prepares the body for "fight or flight". (एड्रेनालाईन)

◦ Correct: ... a surge of adrenaline coursed through her veins ...

• Spelling key: AD + REN + A + LINE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "adrennaline" (double "n"), "adrineline" and "adreneline" all have wrong vowels/letters.

NOTE

• Adrenaline (epinephrine) is secreted by the adrenal glands (located above the kidneys). It raises heart rate, blood pressure and blood sugar during stress or excitement.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. conform.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conform to" means to comply with / behave according to rules, standards or another's way of thinking. The writer does not want to persuade you to conform to his way of thinking. (अनुरूप होना / के अनुसार चलना)

◦ Correct: ... to persuade you to conform to the way the writer thinks or feels.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "affirm" (to state firmly) and Option 2 "confirm" (to verify) do not take "to" in this sense.

• Option 4 "control" does not fit the preposition "to" or the meaning.

NOTE

• The verb "conform" is followed by the preposition "to" (conform to rules/norms). Do not confuse: affirm (assert), confirm (verify), conform (comply).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. between.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "between" is used when referring to two people/things. Here it is "a dialogue between two friends". (के बीच)

◦ Correct: It is really a dialogue between two friends talking about their problems.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "behind" (at the back of), Option 2 "unless" (a conjunction meaning 'if not') and Option 4 "before" (in front of / earlier) do not fit "a dialogue ___ two friends".

NOTE

• Use "between" for two (a talk between two friends) and "among" for more than two (shared among the students). A "dialogue" is a conversation between two parties.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. radical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Radical" (adjective) means thorough, complete or fundamental. A "radical transformation" is a deep, far-reaching change — which fits the idea of changing "the way human beings live". (आमूल-चूल / मौलिक)

◦ Correct: ... there must be a radical transformation in the way human beings live ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "radial" (arranged like rays from a centre) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "avoidable" (able to be avoided) contradicts the need for change.

• Option 4 "highly" is an adverb and cannot directly modify the noun "transformation".

NOTE

• "Radical" can mean fundamental/far-reaching (radical change) or, politically, favouring extreme reform. Synonyms: fundamental, sweeping, drastic, thorough.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. most.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With "the" and a long adjective, we form the superlative with "most". "The most important person" means the single most important person, which fits the emphasis on the teacher. (सबसे — उच्चतम अवस्था)

◦ Correct: The teacher is the most important person in the school ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "much" and Option 3 "more" cannot follow "the ... important" here (comparative "more" would need "than").

• Option 2 "not" reverses the intended meaning.

NOTE

• Superlative of long adjectives: "the most important / the most beautiful". Comparative: "more important than". The word "the" signals the superlative degree.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "of" correctly links "regeneration" with "the mind" — "the regeneration of the mind" (the renewal/rebirth of the mind). (का — संबंध सूचक)

◦ Correct: ... these schools must be centres for the regeneration of the mind.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "under", Option 2 "although" (a conjunction) and Option 4 "off" do not fit the phrase "regeneration ___ the mind".

NOTE

• "Regeneration of" (something) is the standard collocation, like "renewal of", "growth of", "development of". "Of" shows a relationship of belonging or connection.
